faq.a: Khava is associated with the Arabic form حَوَّاء, whose core sense is khava; eve (chechen form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Khava?
faq.a: Khava is associated with Arabic. Khava is the Chechen form of Arabic حَوَّاء (Ḥawwāʾ), the name of Eve.
Yes — the underlying form حَوَّاء is Arabic.
Khava can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Khava should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ḥawwāʾ is not a Quranic personal name, though Eve is referred to in the Quran.

faq.a: In Persian, Khava is rendered حوا and carries the sense حوا، حوا.

faq.q: What are the variants of Khava?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Khava, khava. Script forms are حوا, حَوَّاء, ख़वा.

faq.q: Is Khava a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
